entries.title: What Mezcal is
entries.text: Mezcal is a fungible token protocol on Bitcoin mainnet. Instructions travel as UTF-8 JSON in an OP_RETURN output; balances live on transaction outputs.

entries.title: At a glance: chain, network, genesis
entries.text: Bitcoin mainnet, OP_RETURN carrier, UTF-8 JSON encoding, asset ids of the form block:tx, genesis block 898750, divisibility 0 to 18, u128 amounts.

entries.title: The shape of a payload
entries.text: One JSON object with a required protocol tag and optional edicts, etching, mint, and pointer keys. An edict is asset id, base-unit amount, output index.

entries.title: Bitcoin Universe support
entries.text: Discovery and explorer views are available. The Mezcal marketplace surface is declared read-only in the Core protocol registry. Indexing coverage is partial: no complete mempool feed.

entries.title: 1. Transaction carrier
entries.text: The mezcalstone is taken from the first nulldata output. Push-data chunks after OP_RETURN are concatenated, decoded as UTF-8, and parsed as JSON.

entries.title: 2. Payload grammar
entries.text: Strict validation over five keys: p, edicts, etching, mint, pointer. The protocol tag must be mezcal, https://mezcal.sh, or https://t.me/mezcalbtc.

entries.title: 3. Identifiers, block:tx and 0:0
entries.text: An asset id is the etching block height and the transaction index inside that block. 0:0 inside an edict self-references the asset etched by the same transaction. Genesis is 1:0.

entries.title: 4. Amounts and base units
entries.text: Every amount is a decimal string within the u128 range, expressed in base units. Display amount times ten to the power of divisibility.

entries.title: 5. Etching an asset
entries.text: Name of 1 to 15 lowercase characters, a one code point symbol, divisibility 0 to 18, a premine, and mint terms that may be null. Names are unique; a duplicate etching is ignored.

entries.title: 6. Minting
entries.text: A mint names an asset by id. Cap, height and offset windows, and price terms decide whether it produces anything. A flex mint produces floor of satoshis paid divided by price.

entries.title: 7. Edicts and allocation
entries.text: Edicts run in order and are clamped to the unallocated pool. An amount of zero allocates everything remaining. An edict may target the OP_RETURN output, which burns.

entries.title: 8. Pointer and remainder
entries.text: Whatever the edicts did not allocate goes to the pointer output, or to the first non-OP_RETURN output. There is no implicit change output.

entries.title: 9. Burning
entries.text: Units sent to an OP_RETURN output are destroyed. A cenotaph burns every Mezcal balance carried by the transaction inputs.

entries.title: 10. Cenotaph conditions
entries.text: Eight conditions make a transaction a cenotaph: bad script, unparseable JSON, non-object payload, unknown key, wrong protocol tag, any type or range error, an out-of-range output index, or a block-zero edict id.

entries.title: 11. Order of evaluation
entries.text: Within a transaction: gather input balances, etch, mint, apply edicts, sweep the remainder, then record burns and write balances.

entries.title: The mental model
entries.text: One pool per asset, one pass over the edicts, one sweep of the remainder. That is the whole model.

entries.title: Etching an asset, worked
entries.text: A full etching payload with terms, its byte size, and the decisions that cannot be changed afterwards: name, divisibility, premine, and terms.

entries.title: Minting, worked
entries.text: A mint payload is 33 bytes of JSON. Price terms must be paid by outputs of the same transaction, or nothing is minted.

entries.title: Transferring, worked
entries.text: One edict to the recipient and a pointer to your change output. Forgetting the pointer hands your change to the recipient.

entries.title: Burning
entries.text: There is no burn operation. Burning is a destination: an edict or the remainder aimed at the OP_RETURN output, or a cenotaph by accident.

entries.title: Before you sign
entries.text: Decode the OP_RETURN, check the asset id, check the amount scale, check every output index, check where the remainder lands, check your fee inputs.

entries.title: Support matrix
entries.text: What Bitcoin Universe products support for Mezcal, grounded in the Core protocol registry: discovery supported, marketplace mutations read-only, wallet and inscribe actions declared, indexing available with partial coverage.

entries.title: Terminology
entries.text: Mezcalstone, etching, asset id, edict, pointer, unallocated pool, cenotaph, base units, flex mint, turbo.

entries.title: Indexer semantics: confirmation and mempool
entries.text: State exists only for confirmed transactions, verified against Bitcoin Core block membership. There is no complete Mezcal mempool feed, so coverage is partial and pending activity is never inferred.

entries.title: Reorganization handling
entries.text: A checkpoint of the last confirmed height and hash must still agree with Bitcoin Core. On a mismatch readiness fails, the indexer rewinds at the first changed offset and emits invalidations.

entries.title: Core marketplace behaviour
entries.text: A listing is re-proved against the Bitcoin prevout and the Mezcal authority. The buy OP_RETURN is derived from what was proven and compared byte for byte; mixed tickers are refused.

entries.title: Size and fee notes
entries.text: A mint payload costs 44 output bytes, a transfer with a pointer 89, an etching with terms 198. Using the short protocol tag saves 11 bytes.

entries.title: Limitations
entries.text: Failures are silent, cenotaphs burn, there is no implicit change, names are first-come, and an output index equal to the output count is a cenotaph.

entries.title: Security considerations
entries.text: The payload is unauthenticated text. Never accept a client-supplied payload you are signing for, screen fee inputs, beware display units, and confirm before you rely.

entries.title: Implementation checklist
entries.text: Eleven steps for an indexer that intends to agree with the reference implementation, from the genesis block to reorganization rewind.

entries.title: Valid payloads
entries.text: Nine valid payloads with hex encodings: minimal transfer, whole balance, transfer with change, mint, etch with premine, no operation, deliberate burn, object-form edict, clamped over-allocation.

entries.title: Cenotaph payloads
entries.text: Eleven payloads that burn everything: not JSON, an array, an unknown key, a wrong protocol tag, a numeric amount, an out-of-range output index, a block-zero id, a bad divisibility, symbol, or name, and a missing tag.

entries.title: Payloads that do nothing, safely
entries.text: A mint of an unknown asset, an etching of a taken name, an edict for an asset with no balance, and a transaction with no OP_RETURN at all.

entries.title: Payload validator and builder
entries.text: Paste hex, a whole OP_RETURN script, or JSON and see every field checked against the rules. Or build a byte-correct payload with size and fee notes. Client-side only.

entries.title: What the validator does not check
entries.text: It has no chain state: it cannot tell whether an asset exists, whether a name is taken, whether a mint window is open, or whether your inputs hold the balance.
